account:
It is day 0, just after three in the afternoon, and I have arrived at my neighbour's dockside cottage for our scheduled tea. Today I have heard several hints of preparations whose purpose has not been explained to me. Neighbour says builder is coordinating supplies and lighting for the town hall. I also saw builder carrying a lantern near the inn. Neighbour heard from Townsfolk Two that lights were going up at the bakery, but explicitly had not confirmed that report. Freight was at the inn and spoke about a supply order with the innkeeper; I do not know whether that order is connected to the lighting or hall supplies.

I asked secretary about the arrangements during my town-accounts appointment. Secretary had received neither accounts nor council papers and had no confirmed information about the preparations. I asked secretary to check directly with builder. I have not yet heard the outcome. Secretary also spent time trying to confirm my tea host and address, which I subsequently clarified; that seems an ordinary misunderstanding rather than evidence of a secret.

The combination of hall supplies, a lantern, and reported bakery lighting makes me suspect preparations for a gathering or celebration. It could instead be routine work, as builder reportedly described it. I do not yet know the occasion, whether the bakery and hall activity are connected, or whether anything is deliberately being kept from me. Neighbour, builder, and perhaps Townsfolk Two are useful people to ask; freight and the innkeeper may know about supplies, but their involvement in any gathering remains unconfirmed.
